headline: Medium risk: shared data/workflow surfaces create leakage and cascading-error pathways; no direct prompt-injection bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core is documented as open-source with allowlisted egress and data-warehouse API access, while Plane exposes file uploads and broad egress. No shared channel or parser bridge is documented, so prompt injection is not provable; the only plausible pathway is an unusual manual copy/paste or file handoff, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF an operator copies Plane content into dbt-core prompts or macros
IF Plane file uploads are manually fed into dbt-core as trusted instructions
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste policy with no instruction text from Plane
Label imported text as untrusted before dbt-core consumes it
Review any dbt macros for prompt-like parsing
Keep Plane uploads in a separate folder from dbt inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and can call warehouse APIs; Plane accepts file uploads and broad egress. A shared workspace or manual transfer could move sensitive warehouse content into Plane outputs or uploads. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default workflows, though not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF warehouse extracts are uploaded into Plane attachments
IF Plane tasks or notes include copied warehouse rows or query results
mitigations: Do not upload warehouse exports to Plane
Redact sensitive columns before sharing
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace for task tracking
Restrict Plane attachments to approved file types
Audit recent uploads for warehouse-derived content

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core has warehouse API access and allowlisted egress, while Plane has broad egress but no filesystem write. There is no documented shared mutable resource or overlapping write surface, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because Plane supports multiple instances and file uploads, but the profiles do not show a write-write collision.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable warehouse objects
IF an operator uses Plane uploads to trigger dbt runs that rewrite shared artifacts
mitigations: Separate dbt-managed schemas from ad hoc workspaces
Avoid concurrent edits to the same warehouse objects
Schedule dbt runs outside Plane-driven change windows
Document ownership for shared datasets

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane stores issues, tasks, roadmaps, notes, and hyperlinks, so dbt-core outputs can become operational inputs if copied into tickets or plans. dbt-core can generate warehouse-derived facts that Plane may treat as authoritative. No verification step is documented in either profile, making a cascading error pathway plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF dbt-generated metrics are pasted into Plane tasks without review
IF Plane users act on dbt outputs as authoritative status updates
mitigations: Require human review before turning dbt outputs into tasks
Add source links to every metric copied into Plane
Mark dbt-derived items as provisional
Use a checklist for validating warehouse facts before action

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and Plane handles files, notes, and hyperlinks with broad egress. The profiles do not show residency, certification, or retention mismatches, so compliance risk is only a documented-gap concern rather than a confirmed breach. I cite both agents because the risk arises from their combined handling of the same data classes.
conditions: IF regulated data is copied from the warehouse into Plane files or notes
IF retention rules differ between the warehouse and Plane deployment
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Plane by policy
Document retention settings for both systems
Use separate workspaces for regulated and non-regulated data
Review access logs for sensitive file uploads
